newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty drifts up vs basket, depos rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty drifts up vs basket, depos rise.

text.p: Polish zloty drifted upward toward resistance at three percent from the trading band centre on Wednesday as banks cut currency exposure to take advantage of higher yielding zloty deposits over the weekend.
Dealers said volume remained light on Wednesday and that the zloty would likely remain in its recent band between 2.9 and three percent from parity for the rest of the week.
"The zloty should remain around present levels with strong resistance at 3.05 or 3.00 percent," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, forex dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The zloty closed at 3.03/2.95 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 2.92/2.87 percent close.
It was at 3.0820/40 to the dollar, up from 3.0855/65 on Tuesday and at 1.8070/90 to the mark, up from 1.8080/95.

Dealers said in the longer term the zloty was more likely to lose ground against the basket as zloty-boosting portfolio investments would likely slow after Finance Minister Marek Belka said there was no room to cut the zloty devaluation rate.
"Some investors are bearish on the zloty after minister Belka singalled the crawling peg devaluation constant will not be reduced," said Mateusz Bieniek from Societe Generale.
"The zloty's upside is capped by central bank interntions above three percent from parity so it seems the only way the currency can go is down," Bieniek added.
On the money market one-day deposit rates rose as the market tightened as banks paid for T-bills bought on Monday.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates closed at 22.00/22.50 percent up from this morning's 21.75/21.95 percent.
